definitions.explanation: A behavioral tendency, often unconscious; can refer to good or bad habits, but frequently implies a bad or unusual habit.
Natural wave or curl in hair.

examples.japanese: {爪|つめ}を{噛|か}む{癖|くせ}がある。
examples.english: I have a habit of biting my nails.
examples.notes: 〜癖がある = to have a habit of ~

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{口癖|くちぐせ}は「{まあ|まあ}」だ。
examples.notes: 口癖 = verbal habit, pet phrase

examples.japanese: {悪|わる}い{癖|くせ}を{直|なお}したい。
examples.english: I want to fix my bad habit.
examples.notes: 癖を直す = to fix a habit

notes:
USAGE: {癖|くせ} often has a negative connotation, referring to bad habits or peculiar behaviors. However, it can also be neutral.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{癖|くせ}がある (to have a habit of)
・{癖|くせ}になる (to become a habit)
・{癖|くせ}を{直|なお}す (to fix a habit)
・{口癖|くちぐせ} (verbal habit, catchphrase)
・{悪|わる}い{癖|くせ} (bad habit)

GRAMMAR:
・〜{癖|くせ}に (despite ~, even though ~) - a conjunctive use expressing criticism

CONTRAST:
・{癖|くせ} - habit (often negative or quirky)
・{習慣|しゅうかん} - habit, custom (neutral, established routine)
